issues.what: The family SPA p-values reported as the multiplicity verdict are inflated by an implementation artifact: harness.spa studentises every candidate, and variant 1177 (foundation stop + exit_on_choch_against, which equals the L1 benchmark on all but 8 of 4,452 minute trades / 1 of 826 five-minute trades; per-session gain sd 6.5 INR on minute, 40 INR on 5m) produces a heavy-tailed bootstrap statistic that attains the family max in 302/2000 RC and 396/2000 SPA draws on minute and 755/2000 on 5-minute (its statistic exceeds 17,000 in 37% of 5m draws). Removing the near-duplicates of the benchmark: minute SPA p 0.396 -> 0.322 (RC 0.501 -> 0.448); 5-minute SPA p 0.4965 -> 0.165 (RC 0.5175 -> 0.191; 0.1015 when the 34 variants differing from the benchmark in < 100 sessions are removed). Both remain above the 0.10 threshold, so the FAIL on SPA and the null verdict stand, but the reported 5-minute figure is ~3x the family's true p and the same artifact will affect any harness family that contains a near-copy of its benchmark.
issues.where: OUT/studies/exit_policy/FINDINGS.md sections 3 and 9 ('SPA p 0.396', 'SPA p 0.4965'); findings.json timeframes.*.spa; OUT/harness.py:474-492 (spa: sdb = std + 1e-12 studentisation); 02_c_select.py:105
issues.evidence: Reproduced with the study's own vectors and bootstrap indices (tag 'exit|<tf>'): as run RC p 0.5010 / SPA p 0.3960 (minute), 0.5175 / 0.4965 (5m). Variant 1177 minute: real-difference sessions 7, sd 6.484, bootstrap statistic p90 2.08, p99 4.57, share >= rc_stat 0.134 vs 0.043 for a N(0,1) candidate. Drop 1177: minute RC 0.448 / SPA 0.322. 5m: variants 1177 and 1183 (identical vectors) differ from the benchmark in 1 session; statistic p90 17,863; dropping the 4 variants with < 30 real-difference sessions gives RC 0.191 / SPA 0.165; harness.spa on the reduced family reproduces those numbers. Median of the bootstrap max over well-behaved candidates 1.559 (minute) vs best observed t 1.683: the genuine multiplicity FAIL remains.
issues.fix: Report the SPA p over the family with exact or near-duplicates of the benchmark removed (or floor the studentising sd at a sensible fraction of the benchmark's per-session sd) and state both numbers; flag in harness.py that spa() must not receive candidates whose gain series is a rounding-noise copy of the benchmark. The verdict does not change.

issues.what: The pass-rule check 'diff_top1_gains_removed > 0' is not the pre-registered statistic. BRIEF, README rule 5 and harness.metrics define 'the difference with the top 1% winners removed' (trades whose net is in the top 1%); the study instead removes the top 1% of per-trade policy-minus-Foundation gains, a one-sided trim that is biased negative for any heavy-tailed series (applied to the sign-flipped series it gives -162; the symmetric 1%/1% trim gives +7.46). The pre-registered version, computed by the study itself as diff_top1_winners_removed, is +4.01 (pass) but is omitted from FINDINGS.md's table and from the pass rule. 06_findings.py's docstring states the pass rule was written after learner C's results were read. The 'no candidate' verdict is unaffected because SPA fails regardless (and under the harness GO the book also fails kept_mean_slip8 > 0 at -1313 and DSR p 1.0), but the FINDINGS attribute the failure to a post-hoc metric.
issues.where: OUT/studies/exit_policy/05_evaluate.py:47-50; 06_findings.py:2-6 (docstring) and :29 (pass rule); FINDINGS.md section 1 'Pass rule' and section 9; findings.json pass_rule.checks
issues.evidence: Reproduced from c_pick_minute.npz / c_grid_minute.npz: d = nested - Foundation, mean 86.57; top 45 trades (1%) sum 682,848 vs total 385,417; d[d < q99].mean() = -67.49 (matches); d[net < q99(net)].mean() = +4.01 (matches eval_minute.json diff_top1_winners_removed); symmetric 1% trim +7.46; sign-flipped series under the same metric -162.33. d > 0 on 37.6% of trades (mean +1,756), d < 0 on 62.4% (mean -921); 2022 alone is -62/trade over 1,087 trades.
issues.fix: Apply the pre-registered definition (top 1% winners removed) in the pass rule and report the one-sided gains trim as a descriptive statistic beside it; note in FINDINGS that the pass rule was fixed after learner C's numbers were seen. Keep the null verdict (SPA, slip-8 and DSR fail either way).

issues.what: FINDINGS.md section 5 states the minute learner A was 'not run: the condition ... was not met', while the same document reports B and C beating the Foundation exit OOF (+100.8 / +86.57, i.e. the condition was met) and the FQI is in fact running (pid 6489, 04_a_minute.log). It also says '5minute: not finished', but a_result_5minute.json and the exit-ledger row exit_policy/A exist (OOF mean -902.39, diff -145.34, random pct 62.7, 4/12 blocks, early exits 58%). findings.json has learner_A 'pending' for both and caveats [] despite caveats in the text (ST9 tuned on OOS, exit_rules a new key type).
issues.where: OUT/studies/exit_policy/06_findings.py:109 (hard-coded text); FINDINGS.md section 5; findings.json learner_A, caveats
issues.evidence: ps shows 'python 04_a_fqi.py minute' running; 04_a_5minute.log ends with 'learner A OOF mean -902.39 (Foundation -757.05, diff -145.34)'; exit_ledger.jsonl contains ('5minute','exit_policy/A') 1 row; a_result_5minute.json seconds 902.1.

issues.what: Learner B's inner 3-fold for p* uses interleaved inner test blocks (tr_blocks[i::3]) with a purge over the min..max bar range of those blocks, which removes every block lying between them: the inner training sets are a single block (250-492 trades on minute, 47-82 on 5-minute) instead of ~5 blocks. Not a leak (conservative) and B is not a candidate, but p* is chosen from a model fit on ~10% of the outer training fold, which explains 'never exit' in 2 of 3 minute folds and adds noise the design did not intend.
issues.evidence: Reproduced with controls_minute.npz J and the harness block ranges: minute outer fold 0 inner training sets 492 (block 11) / 361 (block 4) / 1387 (blocks 4,5,10,11) trades out of 2,746; 5-minute outer fold 2 inner training 47 / 82 / 287 out of 556.
issues.fix: Use contiguous inner blocks (e.g. consecutive triples) or purge per test block rather than over the min-max span; report inner training sizes.

issues.what: The random-exit control cannot discriminate any stop-based policy from the benchmark: the Foundation L1 exit itself scores 97.0 (>= 95) on minute and 96.8 on 5-minute against a no-stop uniform-bar exit, so the pass-rule check 'random_pct >= 95' is vacuous for a policy-vs-Foundation comparison. The design panel specified this control and the study reports it honestly beside every policy, but its 'pass' carries no evidence.
issues.where: FINDINGS.md sections 3 and 6 (random_pct column), section 9 pass rule; exlib.py:326-334 (random_control: no stop)
issues.evidence: controls_minute.npz: Foundation pct 97.0, nested 100.0; ST9 (diff -1.1) also 97.0; 5m Foundation 96.8.
issues.fix: Add a control matched to the comparison, e.g. a random exit drawn from the Foundation-stop-floored trajectory, or the session-matched permutation of the per-trade difference; treat random_pct as descriptive.

issues.what: The 1,568 variants and the learners were written to a study-private exit_ledger.jsonl rather than as harness.score rows (README rule 3 / BRIEF: every configuration is a harness ledger row). The study says so and made the vectors harness-compatible, and PBO/SPA/DSR were computed over its own family, but the program-wide ledger (OUT/ledger/trials.jsonl) does not count these 3,173 trials, so any cross-study multiplicity or DSR read through harness.read_ledger() under-counts.
issues.evidence: grep of OUT/ledger/trials.jsonl: 2 rows with family exit_policy (both gate_x_exit); exit_ledger.jsonl: 3,173 rows, vectors/: 3,173 files.
issues.fix: Either register a summary trial count for this family in the harness ledger or have the program-level DSR/SPA scripts read exit_ledger.jsonl too; state the trial count in REPORT.md.

result.verified: Read STUDY_AGENT_BRIEF.md, OUT/README.md, data/README.md, BRIEF.md, DESIGN_PANEL.md exit-policy section (both judges' fixes), harness.py, pre_registration.json, FINDINGS.md, findings.json, all nine study scripts and every log. Re-ran from the study's output files (npz/json/vectors) without touching any file: Foundation L1 means (-1009.61 / -757.05), the 12 nested picks per fold and the OOF means and diffs (-923.04 / +86.57 minute; -818.36 / -61.31 5m), the 11 CPCV path diffs (median 80.19, p5 54.17, min 47.06, 11/11 positive; 5m median -9.41, p5 -65.24, 3/11 positive), in-sample bests (variant 1176, -904.77; 5m variant 1024, -648.81), variants above Foundation (226 / 173), ST9 per position and per lot (-3032.12 / -1010.71; -2747.78 / -915.93), random-exit control mean/p5/p95 and percentiles (Foundation 97.0 / 96.8, nested 100.0 / 88.3), oracles (2560.00 / 1357.95; 2801.47 / 1860.92), the bootstrap CIs with the study's tags ([25.24, 151.11]; [-182.92, 53.4]), PBO ('diff', 12,870 partitions: 0.0866 / 0.1426), SPA and RC p (0.396 / 0.501; 0.4965 / 0.5175), effective trials 1.39 / 1.61 and 957 distinct gain vectors, diff_top1_gains_removed -67.49 and diff_top1_winners_removed +4.01, block means of the gain (10/12 positive). Confirmed the grid's foundation-stop + CHoCH-exit variant equals the L1 label on all but 8 (minute) / 1 (5m) trades, matching parity.json's cap-bar CHoCH counts; the ST9 ladder is marked as tuned on 2026 = OOS everywhere; oracles are labelled upper bounds; per-lot vs per-position is stated; no script reads OOS labels (exlib.Data cuts to T.is_mask; harness.score default split IS). Ledger discipline: exit_ledger.jsonl 3,173 rows = 2 x (1568 + 1 + 1 + 11 + 4 + 1) + 1 (5m learner A), vectors/ 3,173 files; OUT/ledger/trials.jsonl contains exactly the two exit_policy/gate_x_exit rows. Diagnosed the SPA p by replicating harness.spa's internals with the same bootstrap indices (argmax candidate per draw, statistic quantiles, exclusion of near-duplicates of the benchmark) and reproduced learner B's inner-fold purge sizes. The null result is correctly stated and robust: the lead 1-minute policy fails the family SPA even after correcting the near-duplicate artifact (0.322), the 5-minute nested pick fails on its own diff, and no candidate is proposed.
